task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a reported feature of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the delivery volunteers who carry the weekly Fellshore Ledger into neighborhood shops and meeting places. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Fellshore Ledger is a weekly community newspaper distributed in print through local shops, public meeting places and a small volunteer route.
Delivery coordinator Rena Callen sorts bundles by destination in a borrowed room behind the newspaper's office.
The supplied scene describes volunteers checking bundle labels against a paper route sheet before loading bags and a handcart.
The route sheet records copies delivered, not how many people eventually read a copy or pass it to someone else.
The newspaper retains a website, but the print route serves places where readers may encounter the paper without looking for it online.
Callen said, "A bundle is not delivered just because it has left this room. We need to know the shop was open and somebody actually took it in."
Volunteers note closed premises or unused copies from the previous week so the next route can be adjusted.
Returned or undelivered copies are kept separate from the count successfully placed at distribution points.
Shopkeeper Elva Marr keeps a small stack beside the counter where customers wait for service.
Marr said, "People turn first to the notices, then they tell me which meeting I have forgotten."
The Ledger's income combines advertising and reader support; the supplied packet does not disclose its full accounts or claim print distribution is profitable by itself.
The delivery volunteers are not responsible for deciding the newspaper's editorial position or approving articles.
The editorial office handles corrections, and a volunteer who hears a concern passes it back rather than promise a change at the doorstep.
The route has changed as businesses opened, closed or altered their hours, rather than remaining identical from week to week.
New volunteers accompany an experienced delivery worker before taking a route alone.
The coordinator keeps private contact information off the public distribution list.
The community center takes copies for its foyer and does not require readers to attend a particular activity before picking one up.
Bad weather can change delivery timing, and the paper does not guarantee that every outlet has copies at one exact hour.
The borrowed sorting room contains shelves of older issues that volunteers use to answer occasional questions about dates.
The paper has no audited unique-reader total derived from the volunteer route records in this packet.
The current volunteer recruitment asks for help with existing routes rather than announcing a new edition or an expansion into every neighborhood.
The account does not supply any text from another newspaper or assert that the fictional Ledger influenced a particular public decision.

forbidden_additions: Delivered copies equated with unique readers or audited circulation reach.
Volunteers setting editorial policy or guaranteeing corrections.
Standalone print profitability, exact universal delivery times or a new edition.
preserve: The practical work of placing copies where people encounter them.
The distinction between distribution, readership and editorial responsibility.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
